title: kbgit.py publish recomputes the whole projection on every run, most of the hook's 60 s on a long history
goal: kbpublic.project reuses the projection it computed before (refs/kb/published or a cache of source to projected shas under _cache/publish/) and projects only the commits after it, so publish --hook spends seconds, not most of its 60 s timeout, on a history of about a thousand commits of which several hundred are rewritten (each rewritten commit and tree costs a git hash-object process today); TestProjectionReuse in _tools/test_kbpublic.py asserts a second projection of a longer source writes only the new commits and gives the same shas as a full one; found while timing the history scan of BG-7c3sqgcl, where project() of main took longer than the scan itself
